title: kv-cache: adaptive memory manager + eviction priority to reduce fragmentation and spillover
author: Ethan Collins
description:
Motivation: high fragmentation and frequent spillover events under mixed-length workloads were causing unpredictable latency spikes and elevated GPU memory pressure. This PR introduces an adaptive KV cache memory manager and eviction priority system to reduce fragmentation, improve paging behavior, and limit spillover frequency.

Summary of changes: 1) Introduce a compacting allocator for the in-GPU KV cache that runs opportunistically when fragmentation exceeds a threshold. 2) Add an eviction-priority policy that weights entries by recent reuse, sequence-length contribution, and projected reheat cost. 3) Implement a spillover gating mechanism: when host spillover begins to exceed a per-device budget we trigger aggressive transient eviction and compacting to avoid IO storms. 4) Add telemetry (histograms and counters) for fragmentation ratio, compaction runs, spillover bytes/sec, and eviction cost estimates. 5) Tuned scheduling hooks so compaction runs yield to high-priority real-time requests and run during idle windows. 6) Backwards-compatible config knobs exposed via runtime config (compaction_threshold_pct, spillover_budget_mb, eviction_reuse_half_life_ms).

Checklist: - [x] Design doc (linked in PR) - [x] Unit + integration tests covering eviction priority & compaction - [x] Performance benchmarks (microbench + perf-canary runs) - [x] Updated telemetry + dashboards - [x] Feature-flag gated rollout

Why this matters: In long-running serving processes we observed fragmentation ratios > 35% on multi-tenant instances with heterogeneous sequence lengths, leading to repeated spillover and IO contention during peak. The new manager reduces observed spillover events by ~65% in perf-canary runs while keeping median latency within SLO and reducing p99 latency spikes by 30% in mixed workloads.

Compatibility/rollout: Feature is behind a runtime feature flag and defaults to off. We plan a staged rollout: internal perf-canary -> limited customer Dedicated pools -> global. Fall-back is immediate: toggling the flag reverts to prior allocator/eviction.

Notes: Implementation kept ABI-stable: public runtime APIs unchanged. The compactor operates on the same allocation units used by existing KV cache sharding, minimizing code-path churn.
